title: Proposal: `structuredValue` (name TBB) instead of ad hoc `valueAsXXX` attributes

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve? What solutions exist today?

Currently, there is a proliferation of ad hoc attributes on `HTMLInputElement` and other form controls to get the value as useful JS data:
- [`valueAsNumber`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#dom-input-valueasnumber-dev) for numbers
- [`valueAsDate`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#dom-input-valueasdate-dev) for `Date` objects
- `checked` for booleans
- `files` for `<input type="file">`

This doesn't scale. 
- Are we going to create new attributes once `Temporal` ships more broadly?
- Are we going to add `valueAsColor` once the Color API ships?
- What about more complex controls, such as two-handle sliders? The lack of native controls for more complex interactions came up a fair bit in State of HTML, and there is currently no good pattern for it.

### How would you solve it?

A unified attribute that basically means "give me this form control's data in whatever format is most useful", with specifications about individual form controls or input types specifying what that is more precisely. Authors can then detect what type they're dealing with quite easily.

For example, this could be:
- Suitable `Temporal` objects for temporal input types
- `Color` object for `<input type=color>`
- `File` array for `<input type=file>`
- `URL` object for `<input type=url>`
- Numbers for single sliders or number inputs
- Boolean for checkbox
- Checked radio id for radio (regardless of which radio in the group the attribute is dereferenced on)
- Array of option ids for `<select multiple>`
- `{min: number, max: number}` for two-handle sliders
- `{min: Temporal, max: Temporal}` for date range controls 
- and so on. The sky is the limit!

Then, for complex form controls, `value` could be defined as a serialization, and even be lazily evaluated.

In addition to native controls, this also provides a pattern that web components can follow, allowing authors to handle native and WC form controls in one unified way.

### Anything else?

Name ideas:
- `data` (it clashes with `object.data`, but it's not a form control)
- `structuredValue`
- `valueAsData`
